title: Naming Flat Shapes
short: Name squares, circles, triangles, rectangles and hexagons.
trouble: Children say a tilted or upside-down triangle is "not a triangle" because it does not look like the usual picture.

blocks.html: Shapes are everywhere! Let’s name five flat shapes.

blocks.name: k-pic
blocks.cap: A circle, a square, a triangle, a rectangle and a hexagon.

blocks.html: A shape’s name comes from its sides and corners, not from its size, its color, or which way it is turned.
Turning a triangle does not change its 3 sides and 3 corners. So it is still a triangle.

blocks.name: k-pic
blocks.cap: Upside down, skinny or tilted: all of these are triangles.

blocks.title: Upside down
blocks.q: Is an upside-down triangle still a triangle?
steps: Yes. It is still a triangle.

blocks.html: Saying a tilted or upside-down triangle is “not a triangle” because it does not look like the usual picture. Turning never changes a shape’s name. Count the sides to check.
For grown-ups: Go on a shape hunt at home: plates, windows, books, signs. Turn a paper triangle around and ask if it is still a triangle.

sources.name: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics, Kindergarten, K.G.A.2: correctly name shapes regardless of their orientations or overall size
